 There's a missing piece of the puzzle that can't be overlooked.
 By Maurie Backman – Nov 6, 2026 at 12:43PM EST + Fool.com on Share Summarize with AI Key Points
 Social Security benefits are getting a 3.6% COLA in 2027. 
 If you're on Medicare, you can't simply apply that increase to your current benefit and call it a day. 
 If you're someone who gets a large chunk of your income from Social Security, then the program's annual cost-of-living adjustments, or COLAs, are probably pretty important to your finances. Even if you have savings, if you mostly live on Social Security , those boosts might spell the difference between pinching pennies and having more breathing room.
 At this point of the year, there's no need to speculate about how much Social Security benefits are going up in 2027. In mid-October, the Social Security Administration announced that benefits will be getting a 3.6% increase. That's considerably more generous than the 2.8% COLA that arrived earlier this year.
 Image source: Getty Images.
 Now, at first glance, you'd think calculating your specific benefit increase for 2027 would be simple. All you need to do is take your current Social Security check and see what a 3.6% increase amounts to. But for some retirees, the math is not so simple.
 Medicare Part B is the big wild card
 If you're on Medicare and collect Social Security, you may be aware that your Part B premiums are paid out of your monthly benefits directly. What this means, though, is that if the cost of Part B increases in 2027, it will eat into your upcoming COLA, leaving you with less of a net raise.
 Let's say you collect $2,000 a month in Social Security. With a 3.6% COLA, your monthly check rises by $72.
 But what if the cost of Medicare Part B increases by $10 or $15? You'll need to subtract that increase from your previously calculated raise to see how much extra money you'll actually get out of Social Security on a monthly basis.
 And if you're wondering when Medicare will release its official Part B premium for 2027, it's anyone's guess. Last year, that information came out in mid-November. This year's timeline could be similar, but that information could also get delayed.
 It's best not to be so COLA-dependent
 If you're in a position where it's important to know exactly how much money your 2027 Social Security COLA will put in your pocket, it means you might benefit from some financial changes. If money is tight, going back to work part-time could reduce some of your financial stress.
 You may also want to take steps to help your Social Security benefits last longer. Those could include reducing spending in small ways or making bigger changes, like downsizing to a less expensive home.
 Either way, right now, the best you can do is get a ballpark idea of how much more money your Social Security checks will be worth in 2027. You'll need to stay tuned for the big Medicare announcement to get the whole story.
